timing: Complete release Wasm processes with input, output and exit; no MoonX and no startup subtraction
slowdown_policy: The shared-foundation integration accepts the measured small abstraction costs. A ratio above this review boundary is never offset against another workload's gain.
coverage_policy: Compare every built command artifact with a frozen baseline. Every changed artifact needs a registered command profile. Run all registered profiles, including unchanged controls. Missing, failed or unstable evidence cannot pass. Unchanged artifacts do not establish upstream parity.

separate_required_evidence.sort-spill-8m: The pre-foundation baseline exceeded 20 seconds in warmup at -S 1M. Retain that failure. Validate the candidate with the same deadline and compare its bytes with the baseline default-budget sort; this is a repair observation, not an old/new speed ratio.
separate_required_evidence.resources: Observe kernel peak RSS, temporary residue and cleanup separately from timing. Single-pair resource observations are not stability qualification.
separate_required_evidence.correctness: Run the applicable Wasm unit and functional suites, including errors, partial output, cancellation, early exit, Unicode and binary cases. Timing fixture coverage alone is insufficient.

boundaries.retain: Exact imported table values and order, first-use construction without suspension, process-local cached tables, unchanged Unicode/encoding semantics and file-type definitions

Lazy bounded boolean-count construction, ordinary blocks no larger than 256 KiB, mandatory-literal filtering throughout each block, exact delimiter exclusion, assertion and empty-match rejection, cached budget decline, and the existing fallback engines
SIMD/SWAR kernels, fused counts, conservative prefilters and specialized regex semantics
Synchronous borrowed batches, explicit owned records, retained-view lifetime and original read sizes
Bounded output ownership, no asynchronous reuse, no replay after partial failure, prefix flush on read failure, diagnostics order and command formatting loops
Exclusive temporary ownership, exact range reads, independent reverse blocks, page caches and sort run layouts
Immutable execution plans and printer configuration built outside the output loop; explicit type-option errors precede input

Literal eligibility before input discard; decoder and binary policies; bounded unmatched suffix; one EOF completion; original fallback selected before streaming; command-owned search rules and unchanged regex matching priority

Cheap policy decline before reads; preserve multi-byte mandatory-literal rejection and the original read capacity; one begin event; prefix matches only decline optimization and never supply results; prefetched decoded records stay in the original line buffer and precede later read errors; fully resolved bounded matcher before discarding bytes; carry state until a delimiter or actual EOF; chunk phase does not disable sparse exit acceleration

Immutable selected runs and output-failure ordering; branch-free fixed-length anchored Boolean matching; exact EOF acceptance; captures, word/whole-record constraints, branches, repetition and backreferences retain the existing span engine
Catalog ownership separated from parsing, with unchanged option precedence and metadata contracts
Directory lifetime and explicit metadata queries; caller-owned ordering, pruning, links and error precedence
Algorithm parents separated from command cli adapters; digest and record formats, CRC, concatenated members, truncation and partial-output behavior
Typed incomplete/invalid syntax and loop control; independent exit, return and signal state; diagnostics, quoting, redirection and scope
Prepared header ownership and transfer-only execution; profile-specific authentication, framing, redirects, timeout and output cleanup
Explicit adaptive-cache failure state, required capability boundaries, launch policy and aligned/relative tab-stop overflow checks

tests.name: record policies preserve count coalescing and synchronous stop boundaries
synchronous reader summaries preserve events limits binary detection and fallback
plain match spans preserve partial write failure prefixes

strategies.invariant: Count precedes coalesced, synchronous and ordinary execution. Binary scan ownership, raw multiline policy, stop conditions and sink capabilities remain distinct.

tests.name: counting agrees across fragmented literals alternatives decoding and final records
counting preserves matches crossing bulk windows and long unmatched records
counting does not bypass an explicit heap limit
literal streaming keeps nominal reads while declined routes grow records

strategies.invariant: Resolve delimiter exclusion and decoding before discarding bytes; retain the unmatched suffix until a delimiter or actual EOF.

tests.name: audit reused regex probe must retain its nominal read bound
regex count streaming does not finalize a partial record on read failure
adaptive count probes preserve begin denial and decoded replay

strategies.invariant: Probe uses nominal capacity independent of retained storage. Replay owns the original decoder, begins once and delivers complete records before later errors.

tests.name: boolean count preparation is lazy and over-budget rejection is cached
resolved state and transition cell budgets enforce exact boundaries
compact and wide routing observes both sides of its exact threshold
count selection revisits dense sparse and dense inputs on the same matcher

strategies.invariant: Preparation distinguishes uninitialized, declined and ready. Mandatory-literal filtering continues throughout the block.

tests.name: wide count table agrees with compact table for tails offsets and bytes
wide endpoint count and stream kernels agree at every chunk phase

strategies.invariant: Exact transition and exit membership preserve delayed matches, EOF and chunk phase. Endpoint discovery replays transitions to recover the earliest endpoint.

tests.name: boolean discovery ends early while full matches and captures remain greedy

strategies.invariant: Boolean discovery does not replace greedy span or capture semantics; fallback retains the original search interval and priority.

tests.name: grep execution preserves flag priority and contextual span output

strategies.invariant: Static route selection preserves summary flag priority, span output with context, and dynamic binary transitions.

tests.name: whole record batches do not retry a partial output failure
whole record batches preserve cross-chunk records and final tails

strategies.invariant: Commit complete buffered records once; retain cross-chunk tails and never replay a partially failed write.

tests.name: span output flushes a complete and partial record before a read error
span output never retries a partially failed threshold flush

strategies.invariant: Span queue resets before writing; partial input record precedes its pending read error.

tests.name: counting batches retain inverted matches NUL records and final fragments

strategies.invariant: Batch record accounting shares one commit operation without changing incremental cross-chunk accounting.

tests.name: adaptive construction is lazy cached and bounded

strategies.invariant: Short literals use AC; shift plans carry explicit optional AC state and a typed handoff. Construction budget decline is cached.

tests.name: certified skips preserve boolean matching for reused states long tails and all byte classes
record DFA budget exhaustion falls back and keeps subsequent searches correct
record NFA construction includes the exact state budget
record DFA admits 255 and 256 states and rejects a 257th without losing cached rows

strategies.invariant: Certified self-loop skips preserve Boolean semantics; budget failure falls back to the span engine.

tests.name: anchored byte predicates agree with the span engine across all short records

strategies.invariant: Only branch-free fixed-length anchored Boolean matching uses the linear plan; exact EOF acceptance is required.

tests.name: anchored linear plans decline branching and position-sensitive syntax

strategies.invariant: Historical onepass profile names are fallback controls. No general onepass implementation is adopted.

tests.name: failed shared output never replays a partially written prefix

strategies.invariant: Output owns queued bytes, serializes borrowing and consumes failed or cancelled writes without replay.

tests.name: large-row field metadata is bounded and does not alter snapshot storage
field metadata thresholds preserve widths at exact row and byte limits

strategies.invariant: Record retrieval and field traversal share mechanisms while row plans remain bounded and output retains original delimiter semantics.

tests.name: spool cleanup runs once and preserves primary error precedence
cancelled spool operations still clean up once

strategies.invariant: Close the file before directory cleanup, preserve the primary error, and report cleanup-only failure.

tests.name: sort merge reservation leaves useful run space for a one MiB budget
sort temporary parent failure cleans owned runs and preserves output

strategies.invariant: Bound run and merge reservations; the separate spill repair observation is not a passing baseline timing ratio.

tests.name: repeated cache pressure retires an unproductive DFA without retrying rows
Unicode quits never retire later ASCII searches
reverse cache pressure falls back over the original full span
real successful scans amortize pressure before a later unproductive window

strategies.invariant: Retire only after repeated unproductive cache fills. Unicode quit is distinct; productive windows restart accounting. Forward and reverse fallback restart the original query.

tests.name: half and boolean searches prepare neither reverse nor capture storage
deferred fallback preserves low-budget spans earliest endpoints and Unicode
literal engines defer storage without removing extended capture slots

strategies.invariant: Compile both NFAs eagerly to preserve constructor errors and metadata. Prepare non-raising reverse/PikeVM storage once on demand; retain all semantic fallback routes.

tests.name: shared SIMD membership is exact for every singleton byte and both polarities
certified SIMD membership covers every byte and nonzero view offsets
byte-set candidates match scalar membership across all bytes and boundaries

strategies.invariant: Share immutable 256-byte membership packing and lane masks. Fixed-array/view loading, polarity and scalar tails stay with their consumers.
